previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for her second cycle of R-ICE chemotherapy with added rituximab due to EBV viremia in the context of classical Hodgkin lymphoma and common variable immunodeficiency. She had ongoing neck pain and a history of intracranial involvement from lymphoma. Imaging showed response to prior treatment with decreased nasopharyngeal mass size. A lumbar MRI ruled out spinal involvement. She received intrathecal methotrexate for CNS prophylaxis and completed chemotherapy without complications. Her blood counts remained low but stable, requiring monitoring, and her diabetes was managed with insulin during the admission. She was discharged home with filgrastim to support white blood cell recovery and instructions to continue all home medications, including immunoprophylaxis and pain management.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  MRI ___ PHARYNX W AND W/O CONTRAST

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with hx of lymphoma with enhancing
nasopharyngeal mass with cervical biopsy c/w hodgkin's lymphoma, started on
R-ICE chemotherapy, completed 2 cycles  // interval change from previous MRI

TECHNIQUE:  Sagittal T1 whole brain, axial FLAIR whole brain, axial T2 fat
saturation nasopharynx, axial T1 nasopharynx, coronal STIR nasopharynx, axial
DTI whole brain, axial T1 fat saturation postcontrast nasopharynx, coronal T1
fat saturation postcontrast nasopharynx, and axial T1 post-contrast whole
brain sequences were performed. A total of 5 cc of Gadovist intravenous
contrast was administered.

COMPARISON:  MRI of the nasopharynx dated ___, and MRI of the head
dated ___.

FINDINGS: 

Please note that this examination is degraded by patient motion artifact.

There has been interval decrease in size of the large enhancing mass within
the skullbase, right greater than left, with some persistent enhancing
asymmetry seen within the right fossa of ___, right tonsillar pillar,
and the right side of the base of the tongue. The exact size of this mass
remains difficult to measure, as it has an amorphous configuration, and is
additionally challenging to measure due to patient motion artifact.  This mass
is resulting in obstruction of the right sided eustachian tube, and fluid is
seen within multiple right-sided mastoid air cells.

The patient is status post left parietal craniotomy, with expected
postsurgical change. FLAIR signal surrounding the left parietal lobe operative
bed is stable. There is no evidence of slow diffusion or enhancement to
suggest the presence of an intracranial tumor.

The visualized paranasal sinuses, and globes are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION: 

1.  Interval decrease in size of the large enhancing mass within the
skullbase, with persistent enhancing asymmetry seen within the right fossa of
___, right tonsillar pillar, and the right side of the base of the
tongue. Exact size of this mass is difficult to measure given its amorphous
configuration and the presence of patient motion artifact.

2.  No evidence of intracranial neoplasm.

3.  Stable postoperative changes, status-post left parietal craniotomy.
